meta.ogTitle: Share files without an account — no sign-up, encrypted

hero.title: Share files without an account
hero.body: Sending a file shouldn't mean creating yet another account — or asking the other person to. With BIShare there's no sign-up on either side: you share a link, QR code, or 6-character code, and they open it in any browser and download. End-to-end encrypted, up to 10 GB free, links auto-expire.

why.title: Why account-free sharing matters
why.body: Google Drive, Dropbox, and most transfer sites want you signed in — and often want the recipient signed in too, or they hit a wall. That's friction and it's data you didn't need to hand over. BIShare asks for nothing: no email, no password, no profile. The file moves, the link expires, and there's no account trailing behind it.

0.b: Open BIShare, drop a file, and get a link, QR code, and 6-character code instantly. No registration, no email verification — just share.

1.b: The recipient opens the link in any browser and downloads. No account wall, no "request access" — it just works, on phone or computer.

2.b: Links auto-expire after 24 hours, and nearby transfers never upload to a server at all. There's no account, and no file lingering in someone's cloud.

comparison.title: Google Drive vs Email vs BIShare

0.q: Can I really share files without signing up?
0.a: Yes. BIShare needs no account to send or receive. You share a link, QR code, or 6-character code, and the recipient opens it in any browser — no registration anywhere.

1.q: Does the recipient need an account?
1.a: No. Unlike Google Drive or Dropbox, there's no account wall and no "request access" step. They just open the link and download.

2.q: Is it still private without an account?
2.a: Yes — arguably more private. There's no profile tied to your transfer, nearby sends are end-to-end encrypted and never uploaded, and share links auto-expire after 24 hours.

3.q: How big a file can I send without signing up?
3.a: Up to 10 GB free through a share link, with no account. Nearby device-to-device transfers over your own Wi-Fi have no size cap at all.

4.q: What's the catch — is it actually free?
4.a: It's genuinely free with no account. You can install BIShare for the fastest nearby transfers, but sending and receiving via a browser link costs nothing and needs no sign-up.

cta.title: Send a file — no account required
cta.body: No sign-up, no email, no friction for you or the recipient. Get BIShare, or just share a link from the browser.
